players.name: Jalen Williams
players.outlook: Williams is coming off an injury-riddled season in which he was only able to play 33 games at a career-low 28.4 MPG. After an offseason to get healthy, Williams is expected to bounce back to or even surpass the rounded 22 points, 5 rebounds, 5 assists and 2 combined blocks and steals he posted in 2024-25. Still only 25 years old and playing next to Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Chet Holmgren, Williams should still be getting better every season.

players.name: Jalen Suggs
players.outlook: Suggs is looking to build on a season in which he averaged 13.8 PPG and a career-high 5.5 APG across 57 games. He shot just 33.9% from three, but was much better in catch-and-shoot situations, hitting 39.3% of those attempts. Suggs’ defense and playmaking keep him fantasy relevant, but his poor postseason shooting and Anthony Black’s emergence add some risk. Suggs is worth drafting in deeper leagues, but he’s more of a waiver-wire option in shallower formats. His fantasy value could improve if Orlando keeps him in more of an off-ball role.

players.name: Kristaps Porzingis
players.outlook: Porzingis is one of the elite per-minute producers of his generation, but injuries have consistently derailed his availability and is already out for training camp. Porzingis missed 50 games last season and 40 the season before, and has missed at least 16 games in nine straight seasons. He is slotted to be the Warriors' starting center this season, and when he plays he will produce, but he is risky to draft in fantasy leagues before the late-middle rounds at the earliest.

players.name: Keegan Murray
players.outlook: Murray enters the season as Sacramento’s likely starting power forward after an injury-plagued fourth season. He averaged 14.0 PPG, 5.7 RPG and 1.6 BPG last season, but shot a career-low 27.7% from three. His defensive production gives him fantasy value even when the shot isn’t falling, while a return to his earlier shooting form would raise his ceiling considerably. Murray still has competition for minutes in Sacramento’s frontcourt, but his two-way role should keep him involved. He’s worth a late-round flier in fantasy drafts.

players.name: Egor Demin
players.outlook: Demin enters his second season after averaging 10.3 PPG, 3.2 RPG and 3.3 APG while shooting 38.5% from beyond the arc as a rookie. He was even better on catch-and-shoot attempts, hitting 40.5%, and showed more ability to attack the rim and create off the dribble during Summer League. With Mikel Brown Jr. and Julius Randle handling more of the offense, Demin should get a ton of opportunities off the ball. Plantar fasciitis remains a concern, but he’s a player fantasy managers should take a late round flier on if his scoring and playmaking continue to develop.

players.name: Shaedon Sharpe
players.outlook: Sharpe faces a lengthy absence after undergoing surgery to repair the lateral meniscus in his right knee. He averaged 20.8 PPG, 4.3 RPG, 2.6 APG and 1.4 SPG in 50 games last season, but won’t be reevaluated until late February. A March return is possible if his recovery goes well, though there’s no guarantee he’ll be ready by then. Sharpe is difficult to draft in standard leagues, but his scoring upside makes him a worthwhile stash for the 2027-28 season for this in keeper formats.

players.name: Cason Wallace
players.outlook: Wallace enters the season positioned for a larger role after starting 58 of 77 games last season. In those starts, he averaged 9.3 PPG, 3.1 RPG, 2.9 APG and 2.1 SPG. With Luguentz Dort no longer in Oklahoma City, Wallace has a clear path to becoming a full-time starter. His scoring ceiling may be limited, but Wallace’s steals, threes and increased playing time make him an intriguing target at the end of your draft, especially in category leagues.

longterm.outlook: Poeltl enters this season as the Raptors starting center after back issues limited him to 46 games last season. The early news is encouraging, with the Raptors saying he is moving well and looks good ahead of training camp. At his best, Poeltl is a steady source of rebounds, efficient scoring and defensive stats, as he averaged 14.5 PPG and 9.6 RPG while shooting 62.7% from the field in 2024-25. The concern is durability after last year’s back problems. Poeltl is worth a late-round pick in deeper leagues if his health holds up.

longterm.name: Keegan Murray
longterm.outlook: Murray enters the season as Sacramento’s likely starting power forward after an injury-plagued fourth season. He averaged 14.0 PPG, 5.7 RPG and 1.6 BPG last season, but shot a career-low 27.7% from three. His defensive production gives him fantasy value even when the shot isn’t falling, while a return to his earlier shooting form would raise his ceiling considerably. Murray still has competition for minutes in Sacramento’s frontcourt, but his two-way role should keep him involved. He’s worth a late-round flier in fantasy drafts.

longterm.name: Isaiah Stewart
longterm.outlook: Stewart joins the Grizzlies after averaging 10.0 PPG, 5.0 RPG and 1.6 BPG while shooting 55% from the field for the Pistons last season. He also shot 33.3% from beyond the arc on 2.1 attempts per game, giving him some floor-spacing ability. Stewart should have a steady reserve role behind Zach Edey and can play both frontcourt spots. His defense, rebounding and blocks give him some fantasy appeal, but his ceiling depends on minutes.

longterm.name: Jerami Grant
longterm.outlook: Grant arrives in Memphis after averaging 18.6 PPG, 3.5 RPG and 2.1 APG while shooting 45.3% from the field with the Blazers last season. He remains a useful source of scoring and threes, but his modest rebounding and assist numbers limit his overall fantasy ceiling. Grant’s role could also fluctuate as the Grizzlies gives significant opportunities to young players like Cameron Boozer and Cedric Coward. He’s best viewed as a waiver wire option in standard leagues.

longterm.name: Scotty Pippen Jr.
longterm.outlook: Pippen Jr. enters the season competing for a significant role in Memphis’ backcourt following the Ja Morant trade. He averaged 11.4 PPG, 4.7 APG and 1.9 SPG in just 21.2 MPG last season, though toe injuries limited him to just 10 games. Pippen has produced when given starter-level minutes, averaging 14.2 PPG and 5.7 APG across 21 starts in 2024-25. Ty Jerome may open the season as the starter, but Pippen’s assists and steals give him intriguing upside.
